fibre.sample: stratified sample of 79 of 281 women's styles (959 feed records; vendor 'Mother Denim' and tag 'Division: Womens' only, less bags, belts, hats, scarves, socks,

craft_evidence.owned: yes — MOTHER Maker, a Los Angeles sewing contractor acquired June 2023, 50+ employees, about 20% of total sewing capacity (house claim)
craft_evidence.makers: own unit named (MOTHER Maker); other LA sewing contractors and wash houses unnamed
craft_evidence.mills: no — 'mills the founders have worked with for over 20 years', none named
craft_evidence.madein: ~72% (57 of 79 sampled pages say 'Made in Los Angeles'); house says 94% of denim and over 90% of all manufacturing is LA
craft_evidence.heritage: no dated founding on the craft page; LA denim-trade preservation argument with cited employment data
craft_evidence.process: partly — 1–3 year fabric development with wear-testing; QC staff placed in facilities; no step-by-step making
craft_evidence.reasoning: An owned sewing unit (MOTHER Maker, acquired 2023) is named and sized, and Los Angeles making is stated on about 72% of product pages and claimed for over 90% of production. But the owned unit does about a fifth of the sewing, and the mills, other contractors and wash houses go unnamed. That is a 3. The case for 4 is the owned unit plus the near-total LA production claim.
